title: The hottest and coldest places ever measured
examples: What is the hottest temperature ever recorded?
Where is the coldest place on Earth?
What is the coldest town where people live?

explain.say: On a hot summer day you might feel 35 degrees. On a snowy day, maybe minus 5. But how hot and how cold can Earth really get? Look at the two record holders on the board.

draw.text: The hottest and coldest places ever measured

explain.say: On the left is Death Valley in California, USA. In July 1913 the air reached 56.7 degrees Celsius, the hottest ever measured. The valley is low and deep, so hot air gets trapped like in an oven. Can you find the number?

On the right is Vostok, a research station in Antarctica. In July 1983 it fell to minus 89.2 degrees Celsius. It is high up and in total darkness during the polar winter. Why do you think July is cold there?

Because July is winter in the south half of the world! Now look at the verdict: the gap between the two records is almost 146 degrees. That is the whole gap from freezing water to boiling water, and almost half as much again!
Wonderful! Wow fact: in Oymyakon, a village in Siberia, Russia, people live with winters below minus 50, and the temperature once dropped to about minus 68 degrees.

faq.q: What is the hottest temperature ever recorded?
faq.a: The World Meteorological Organization lists 56.7 degrees Celsius at Furnace Creek in Death Valley, USA, on 10 July 1913. Some scientists question it, but it is the official record.
asks: Where is the hottest place on Earth?

faq.q: Where is the coldest place on Earth?
faq.a: The coldest air temperature measured at a weather station is minus 89.2 degrees Celsius at Vostok Station, Antarctica, on 21 July 1983.
asks: What is the coldest temperature ever?

faq.q: What is the coldest town where people live?
faq.a: Oymyakon in Siberia, Russia, is often called the coldest lived-in place. Its temperature once fell to about minus 68 degrees Celsius.
asks: Where do people live in the coldest cold?

faq.q: Why is Death Valley so hot?
faq.a: It is a deep, narrow valley below sea level, with dry air and bare rock. The sun heats the ground and the hot air is trapped by the mountains around it.

faq.q: Why is July winter in Antarctica?
faq.a: Earth is tilted. In July the southern half leans away from the Sun, so it has winter, and near the South Pole the Sun does not rise at all for months.
asks: Why are seasons opposite in the south?

facts: The official highest air temperature is 56.7 °C, recorded at Death Valley, California, on 10 July 1913.
The lowest air temperature measured at a station is −89.2 °C, at Vostok Station, Antarctica, on 21 July 1983.

quiz.say: On which continent is the coldest temperature ever measured?
quiz.show: On which continent is the coldest temperature ever measured?
quiz.why: Vostok Station in Antarctica measured minus 89.2 degrees Celsius in 1983.

wrong.0: Siberia in Asia is very cold, but not as cold as Antarctica.
wrong.2: Europe has never come close to that cold.

quiz.say: Why was it so cold at Vostok in July?
quiz.show: Why was it so cold at Vostok in July?

options.show: It was winter in the southern half of Earth
options.say: It was winter in the southern half of Earth

options.show: The station was by the sea
options.say: The station was by the sea
